children.approach: Theorem A: for an interval J of length e in Z/nZ, the 2^{e-1} monomials of A_n with support J are indexed by orientations eps of J's internal edges; a_{J,eps} acts as the cylindric e-ribbon addition at min J of height |eps|. Hence R_e(t) = sum_J sum_eps t^{|eps|} a_{J,eps} in A_n[t].

children.reason: NOT AN INVOLUTION PROBLEM.  The classical argument it was modelled on (Q75 thm:A) uses no involution: it uses a closed-form pairing whose factor (1+t)^{c-1} annihilates every disconnected shape at t=-1.  The cylindric lift (thm-C1-splitting-identity) is the same shape -- sum_b t^b h_{e-b} e_b = sum_I sum_eps t^{|eps|} (1+t)^{r(I)} a_{I,eps} -- and the cancellation is carried by (1+t)^{r(I)}, where the (1+t) is the free choice of which factor the LAST generator of each run goes into.  An involution would have had to pair states; the actual mechanism pairs SPLITTINGS of a fixed monomial, which is why no involution on states was found.

children.approach: If I' cap I'' is nonempty then a_{I',0} a_{I'',1} = 0.  Proof: a_{I',0} EMPTIES every site of I' (each run [i,i+l-1] needs i+1..i+l empty before and leaves i..i+l-1 empty after), while a_{I'',1} REQUIRES every site of I'' occupied.  Verified 27846 overlapping pairs, 2<=n<=6, all k: 0 violations.

For a disjoint split I = I' u I'', a_{I',0} a_{I'',1} = a_{I,eps} with eps_s = [s in I''] for every edge index s.  Edges of I are indexed by I minus L(I), where L(I) is the set of run-last sites, |L(I)| = r(I).  So eps determines the membership of every edge-indexing site and leaves the r(I) run-last sites FREE: each fibre has 2^{r(I)} splits, with generating function t^{|eps|}(1+t)^{r(I)}.  Verified 22776 splits, 2<=n<=7, all k: 0 violations.

CYLINDRIC SPLITTING IDENTITY.  For 1<=e<=n-1, as operators on the sum of QH*(Gr_{kn}): sum_{b=0}^{e} t^b h_{e-b} e_b = sum_{|I|=e} sum_eps t^{|eps|} (1+t)^{r(I)} a_{I,eps}.  This is the cylindric lift of Q75 thm:A, and it absorbs all three of its lemmas (2x2 kills splittings; splittings factor over components; a ribbon has exactly two splittings).  At t=-1 it REPROVES the sub-degree-n half of Postnikov's lem:e-h-commute-in-AN.  Verified 2<=n<=7, all 0<=k<=n, all e<=n-1, exact in Z[q,t]: 0 violations.

R_e(-1) = sum_{b=1}^{e} (-1)^{b-1} b h_{e-b} e_b in A_n, for 1<=e<=n-1.  Proof: differentiate thm-C1-splitting-identity in t at t=-1.  Every I with r(I)>=2 keeps a factor (1+t) and dies; the survivors are exactly r(I)=1, i.e. the INTERVALS, i.e. R_e(-1) by thmA.  The same derivative in Lambda is the classical p_e = sum_b (-1)^{b-1} b h_{e-b} e_b, so the classical expression of p_e in h and e is valid verbatim on the cylinder in degrees <= n-1 -- which is why no wrap term can appear below e=n.  Verified 2<=n<=7, all k, all e<=n-1: 0 violations.

h_j = M_{sigma_j} for 0<=j<=n-1 and e_b = M_{sigma_{1^b}} for 0<=b<=n-1, with sigma_j = 0 for j>n-k and sigma_{1^b} = 0 for b>k.  Postnikov cor:pieri-AN (ll.2935-2947, read at source) covers only 1<=j<=n-k and 1<=b<=k; the extension to the full range is the vanishing argument: e_b = 0 for b>k since a_{I,1} needs I inside S and |S|=k; h_j = 0 for j>n-k since a_{I,0} needs j pairwise-distinct empty sites and S has only n-k.  Verified 2<=n<=8, all k: 0 violations.

GAP (G3) SETTLED.  On QH*(Gr_{1,n}), R_e(t) = R_e(0): t-free (a single bead jumps over nothing). On QH*(Gr_{n-1,n}), R_e(t) = t^{e-1} R_e(1): the target of a legal move is the unique gap, so all e-1 intermediate sites are beads and the height is always e-1.  So at the boundary the t-line collapses to a MONOMIAL and no value of t can be distinguished: the uniqueness question is vacuous, not merely untested. This is a rank degeneracy of the Hall-Littlewood grading, NOT a statement about P^{n-1}.  The two cases are exchanged by the duality cor:duality, consistently.  Verified 3<=n<=8, all e.

Q253 VERDICT (PROVE 2026-09-24 c2).  AKO 2311.07382 thm:cylindricMNRule and Korff-Palazzo 1804.05647 eqref{cylSchur} are NOT the same theorem.  AKO expand s_D over stacked-ribbon data on D; KP expand s_D over cylindric-ribbon data on the CONJUGATE D'.  Classically the two coincide because omega(s_{lam/mu})=s_{lam'/mu'}; cylindrically omega(s_D) != s_{D'}, so they part company.  Same ribbon sets, same signs; they differ ONLY on fully wound steps, by the factor -k/(n-k) -- the two sides of level-rank duality.  AKO's hedge 'a similar formula seems to appear' is correct as a hedge, false as an identification.

This is the structural reason the two rules cannot be transported into each other by conjugation, and it is a finite exact computation refuting a universal statement.

ERRATUM in AKO 2311.07382 (src l.1182-1187).  They define the height of a stacked ribbon TWICE -- 'sum of the heights of its constituents' and 'number of vertical edges of an extended ribbon' -- and assert equivalence.  The two differ by l (the path must traverse one vertical edge at each of the l junctions), so the quoted closed form ht=l*y+ht(F) carries the wrong sign whenever l is ODD.  Correct: ht = l*(y+1)+ht(F).  Their OWN worked example ex:mnrule uses the correct value (annotated 'height 3', not 2) and its printed p-expansion is right -- I reproduced it exactly from CSSYT.  So the prose formula contradicts the example, and the example wins.  Verified 0/797 regions and 0/874 multi-part (D,nu) pairs; as-stated fails 174/797.  PROVED, not merely verified: it is equivalent to Korff 1906.02565 lem:cylMNrule(i) (per-winding factor (-1)^{k-1}), which he proves from H_{nu_i+n}=(-1)^{k-1} q H_{nu_i}.

ERRATUM in Korff-Palazzo 1804.05647.  chi_{lam/d/mu}(nu), as literally defined (sum over cylindric ribbon plane partitions weighted by the pure sign (-1)^{ht-1}), is SHORT BY A FACTOR k for each part of nu consumed by a FULLY WOUND cylindric ribbon.  Minimal counterexample: n=4,k=2,lam=mu=(0,0),d=1 -- a single circular ribbon -- and nu=(4): the definition gives -1, eqref{cylSchur} requires -2.  With multiplicity k: 0 mismatches / 16791 coefficients; as stated: 439; with n-k: 425.  WHERE IT WENT: the multiplicity is in their PROOF ('P*_r adds all possible ribbons of length r') and their lem:CR asserts a unique starting diagonal a only under r not in nN -- exactly the case excluded there is the one carrying the degeneracy, and a ribbon plane partition records shapes, not shapes-with-a-marked-starting-diagonal.  VERIFIED, NOT PROVED.
